A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SConU research work, with complete main text, references, and Appendices A–E. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison; 21 of the 24 pages are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM experiments on sampling-size calibration, miscoverage, conditional coverage, and prediction efficiency in Section 4 and Tables 1–5, with additional cross-domain results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their results in Section 4 and Appendix E, including comparisons of basic ConU, SConU, and SConU-Pro.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same two conformal p-values, outlier rejection procedures, calibration-set maintenance, and minimum-risk calculation. The conformal procedures in Appendix D are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, MMLU-Pro, MedMCQA, TriviaQA, and CoQA, with the same subject coverage and single-domain, cross-domain, closed-ended, and open-ended QA scenarios.

E2.justification: The basic ConU comparator remains in the same comparisons against SConU and SConU-Pro, including Table 2 and the appendix comparisons in Figures 5–9. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same data selections, calibration/test splits, model configurations, prompts, sampling settings, and evaluation metrics. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 retain the analyses of uncertainty-score components, sampling size, split ratio, outlier detection, and model performance. The semantic-deduplication analysis in Table 5 and cross-domain analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: The 100-trial reporting, means and standard deviations, Table 2 medians, and Figure 1 standard-deviation bands are unchanged. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-estimation information is added.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and findings in the main-text result tables and Appendix E are unchanged. Sampling-calibration outcomes, miscoverage rates, prediction-set sizes, and plotted cross-domain trends all match.

T1.justification: Equation (4) is reformatted using a stacked fraction with the same mathematical meaning. The minimum-risk derivation in Section 3.2 and mathematical arguments in Appendices A and C remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about significance testing for uncertainty outliers, minimum manageable risk, marginal coverage, prediction efficiency, and approximate conditional coverage.

C2.justification: Interpretations of exchangeability, calibration reliability, conditional coverage, and semantic redundancy are unchanged. The Limitations paragraph retains exactly the same discussion of excluded test samples and future work on nonexchangeable data.

D1.justification: The code-availability footnote, dataset access links, prompt examples, generation hyperparameters, and implementation descriptions in Appendices B and D are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgment supplies no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to existing conformal methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Acknowledgments section between the Conclusion and Limitations, identifying funding support for three authors. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the scientific prose and remaining organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Equation (4) changes from slash division to a stacked fraction, with localized mathematical spacing and text reflow on page 5. The acknowledgment shifts the Limitations paragraph downward on page 9. Figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution and makes localized typesetting adjustments. The scientific reasoning, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, including all appendix material. These small editorial refinements do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
